full_judgment:
1. Whether on the facts and in the circumstances of the case, the Taxes Appellate Tribunal was justified in law to hold that the assessment made on 30.06.1985 was not barred by limitation. 

 3. Whether in the facts and circumstances of the case, even if, assuming that the notice under section 34 served on 25.12.1985 was a valid one whether the Taxes Appellate Tribunal was right in maintaining that the assessment made on 30.06.1985, that is, beyond one year from the date of service on such notice was not barred by limitation. 

 14. The contention of the applicant that the assessment was barred by limitation is also misconceived and contrary to the pro-vision of law inasmuch as section 34(1 A) does not provide for any time limit and such provision as laid down in section 34(2) proviso (III) is not attracted because a notice in such case could be served at any time and assessment could also be completed at any time without any limitation whatsoever. Clause (a) of sub-section (IA) of section 34 clearly lays down that if the assessee fails to comply with notice under sections 22 (1) and 22(2) notice under section 34(1) can be issued at any time. The provision of sub-section (2) of section 34 prescribes a period of limitation for assessment of the assessee other than those who did not file return under sections 22 (1) and 22(2).
